title: Wald Inference for Quantile Treatment Effects at Critical Weak Overlap via Boundary Transport
banked_reason: D0.5.G delivered tier incremental below field floor: paper_score_ceiling 6.4 < 7.4; sharp minimax variance and matching constant converse remain open.
gap_reasons: It does not prove that the transported coefficient is minimax-sharp, identify the optimal augmentation, or match its achievability result with a variance-constant converse; the lower theorem fixes only the rate and also requires explicit witness-compatibility restrictions.

The contribution remains confined to one quantile under a known scalar power-law propensity chart with bounded outcomes, without evidence that the transport rule remains useful for estimated or multivariate propensities.
D0.5.G projected paper-score gate: paper_score_ceiling 6.4 < 7.4, so the graded tier 'field' is capped at 'incremental'.
proof_attempt_summary: D0 discharged the critical-window raw-IPW QTE law, same-sample Wald inference, an adjacent-band transported estimator with strictly lower variance, and a rate lower bound; the typed math and rubric panels passed without findings. The cold general referee graded the delivered package incremental because the sharp efficiency constant, optimal augmentation, and matching constant converse remain open, and the result covers one quantile in a narrow known-propensity design. The independent validity gate found no credible same-scope repair to the operator's field floor.
tldr: A normalized raw-IPW QTE is a valid critical-window baseline at rate \(r_n=\sqrt{\log n/n}\), with variance \(V(P,\lambda)=2v_1B(\lambda)/f_1(q_1)^2\). Under the same boundary-CDF smoothness class, an explicit adjacent-band transported QTE with cutoff \(g_n=n^{-1/4}\) is uniformly Gaussian and has the strictly smaller coefficient \(V_{\mathrm{tr}}(P,\lambda)=2v_1B_{1/4}(\lambda)/f_1(q_1)^2\). Its same-sample cutoff sandwich is ratio consistent and yields honest Wald coverage. The observed-law construction still fixes the critical rate, while the sharp smoothness-aware minimax constant and optimal augmentation remain open.
gap: Fixed-law weak-overlap QTE theory identifies stable and Gaussian domains but leaves the local index-two crossover, uniform quantile inversion, and feasible critical studentization unresolved. Existing weak-overlap Wald theorems concern clipped mean scores, while regular QTE process theory assumes conventional overlap.
fill: The project derives the explicit crossover variance, proves the required local weighted-CDF and Bahadur lemmas, validates an ordinary untruncated same-sample sandwich uniformly, diagnoses the finite-variance normalization discrepancy, and supplies an observed-law lower benchmark on a rich smooth subclass.
